assignments.package_label: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הַצַּדִּיק, וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד
assignments.reason: This node — Torah study and good speech that one speaks — is the active holy practice that embodies the Torah/chesed domain. Its essential nature is the engagement with Torah (לִמּוּד הַתּוֹרָה) combined with sanctified speech (דִּבּוּרִים טוֹבִים). Torah study is the core identity of Package 2, where Oral Torah, the tzaddik, and torat chesed share the same essential nature as the living divine teaching-presence. The 'good speech' component is the positive, holy actualization of speech — the opposite of the harsh, unsweetened gevurot. The node belongs in the Torah/holiness domain by its intrinsic character: it names the very practice through which Torah she-be'al peh is activated and transmitted, which is the defining activity of Package 2.

assignments.package_label: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הַצַּדִּיק, וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד
assignments.reason: This node — the sweetening of the speech that are the gevurot — names the redemptive outcome in which harsh gevurot are transformed into their positive form. Although the node's description references gevurot (Package 1), its essential nature is the sweetening (הַמְתָּקָה), which the teaching explicitly identifies with the chesed/Torah domain: the tzaddik inclines toward chesed (מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד) and transforms the harsh speech into Torah and torat chesed (line 9). The sweetened state IS the Torah domain realized — the gevurot converted into teaching. The node belongs in Package 2 because its essential character is the positive transformation toward holiness, not the raw gevurot themselves.
